steps.content: At this point in the war report, words could no longer express his joy. Brock sprang up, spinning in a clumsy, ecstatic circle, bobbing and jumping around his tent while humming a wildly off-key tune.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: We won, we won, oh YES, we won! Long live DisCity, long live the Guerrillas! Brock's command win win win—

steps.speaker: Messenger
steps.content: Boss!
A messenger ducked through the tent flap, his breath coming in ragged gasps.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Manners, rookie! You don't just enter a room, you REQUEST to enter a room! Did Dravyn teach you nothing?
The moment he was discovered, Brock spun around and snapped to attention. He scolded with feigned sternness, his face turning bright red as he desperately tried to think of an excuse.
The messenger, however, clearly couldn't wait for any of this.

steps.speaker: Messenger
steps.content: There's no time! Captain, you must hurry. Major Dravyn is in trouble. Andohar... And Andohar—
Immediately, Brock was alert.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Andohar? What's that arms dealer up to now?!

steps.speaker: Messenger
steps.content: Andohar's been hiding a superweapon. The Major's trying to handle it, but... he's never seen anything like that either. The Major—
Bang bang! Bang!
A series of gunshots pierced the air. Brock's eyes widened in shock. He'd know that sound anywhere—it was Dravyn's favorite weapon, a Browning M1910 from the old world.

In an instant, that brutal image consumed him again: the Speaker, gunned down from behind. Eight times. A tremor shook Brock's core, his head throbbing with a sudden, violent heat. Snatching the gun from the table, he stormed out.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Damn it! Don't die, Dravyn!!
[Scene Change] Armory

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Dravyn!
Brock charged into the armory, and a rush of relief crashed over him—his friend was still alive.
But that relief shattered as he saw the officer's face, contorted with rage, clutching a gun whose barrel still smoked.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: ...Look at the trouble you've brought upon us, Brock.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: ...Huh?
The guerrilla commander in a standard-issue military uniform, huh...
Hehe. Someone at DisCorps is being very naughty, aren't they? Should I go tell on you?

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Who's there?!
A shadow fell over his head from above, followed by a childish voice.
[Small CG 1]

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: My name is <color=#fb9259>Catherine Augustus</color>. Of the <color=#fb9259>Andohar family</color>. You know, the arms dealer you cheated? I'm Andohar's youngest daughter.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I hitched a ride in one of the weapons crates, all the way into you rebels' hideout. And now I've seen all your cards. Your gear is a decade out of date, you have zero superpowers between you, and frankly, with that scrap metal you're carrying... catching me isn't an option.

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: If you'd rather the metropoles not find out about your little secrets, let's make a deal. I have a few conditions.

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Why are you still talking to her? She's clearly not a normal human!

Dravyn seized an opening and fired two more shots. Catherine didn't even blink. The bullets halted abruptly, only inches from her body, their momentum dying as if they'd slammed into a wall of invisible mud.
It was only then that Brock's brain caught up. The girl wasn't just perched on some random crate. She was casually seated atop his prized, second-hand missile, hovering in mid-air.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Wait, is this magic? Brat, you—

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: I'm 11 years old, you old fossil. I'll ask one more time: Are we making a deal or not?
She raised her hand—
[Small CG 2]
Several more missiles rose into the air, spinning 720 degrees. Brock's face went pale with terror, his eyes nearly popping out of his head.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Okay! Okay!! Just don't ride my missiles! How am I supposed to pay for them if they break?! Wait, stop playing with them!

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: I agree, I agree, alright?! What do you want? Dravyn, put that gun down NOW!!

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Heh, I've come all the way to your headquarters. Isn't what I want obvious?
[Small CG 3]

steps.speaker: Catherine
steps.content: Let me join the army! Teach me how to fight! Take me to a real battlefield! I can't wait to become a DisCity general!

steps.speaker: Dravyn
steps.content: Just kill her.

steps.speaker: Brock
steps.content: Hold on, HOLD ON—!

On October 22, N.F. 65, the WhiteSands Guerrillas operating outside DisCity captured a special prisoner—a young girl who had traveled undetected even by the Andohar caravan.

She possessed extraordinary abilities that defied conventional understanding. At the time, it was unclear whether she was a superhero like those depicted in television stories, or a bio-engineered weapon developed through the advanced technology of the metropoles.
Years later, such individuals would be formally classified as <color=#fb9259>Sinners</color>—a manifestation of Mania's side effects.
Likewise, history would eventually mark this day as the first encounter between the three generations of leaders from DisCity's old military era.
